text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Swiss health spending almost doubled between 1985 and 1995, a study of the Federal Office for Statistics wrote.
- The number of Swiss workers organised in labour unions has been declining since 1991. Most workers leave their union as soon as they lose their job.

- Swiss banks lost lost 42 billion Swiss francs on bad domestic loans between 1991 and 1996. The three biggest banks -- UBS, Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Bank Corp -- posted the heaviest losses, writing off 12.5 percent of all domestic credits during the period.
- Swiss Federal Banking Commission president Kurt Hauri confirmed earlier statements that an informal survey of Swsis banks had found no trace of funds held by Zaire's president Mobutu Sese Seko.

- Citizens of the small mountain canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden will vote this weekend on whether they want to hold a referendum on abolishing the so-called Landsgemeinde, a centuries-old tradition of gathering outdoors to vote publically on cantonal issues.

- A Berne commission charged with revising Switzerland's constitition narrowly rejected a proposal to remove the right to strike from the list of guaranteed rights. Conservative parties in the four-party government coalition had sought to limit workers' ability to walk out.
- The Swiss government may increase the value added tax in Switzerland, now at a maximum 6.5 percent, by one percentage point in order to cover a deficit in the national pension fund.

- Some 1,350 employees of the European Centre for Nuclear Research (Cern) near Geneva protested against wage cuts. Staff organisations fear that lower salaries would make it more difficult to recruit new top scientists.
